messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance landscape & next steps — streaming p95 targets + MOP checklist

Hi Liam / infra team —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and to lock the next steps so we can size a realistic tryout environment. Thanks again for walking us through the current setup.

Top pain points we heard
- Intermittent tail-latency spikes for streaming inference when concurrent browser sessions hit >= 120 concurrent users (p95 currently ~1.1s, p99 spikes to 5–8s).
- Throughput bottleneck tied to your current batching layer; requests are sent individually from edge which saturates CPU on the routing tier.
- KV cache miss amplification during cold-starts for new sessions (model context windows spike token work).

Current stack (as discussed)
- Frontend: React web app using a websocket streaming client.
- Edge: NGINX + lightweight routing layer (Go) running on Kubernetes, CPU-bound during burst.
- Inference: self-hosted 4x A100 nodes behind Triton (model = open-llama-9B variant), KV cache implemented in-process.
- Telemetry: Prometheus + Grafana; logs forwarded to ELK for retention.

Success criteria for a POC / trial
- Sustained p95 streaming latency <= 600ms at 100 RPS sustained with 120 concurrent sessions (target for main product flows).
- No p99 higher than 2.5s for the same profile.
- Cost estimate showing <= 40% uplift vs your current on-prem run cost for the same traffic (we'll provide a projection).
- Clear rollback/fallback plan to your current Triton endpoints.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share a short traffic sample and the Prometheus query snippet that yields the p95/p99 numbers you referenced? (we can plug this into our evaluation dashboard).
2) Confirm the exact model variant and config (sequence length, batch size used today).
3) Procurement: procurement@finlytics.com — can you confirm if a non-prod PoC contract (60-day) is acceptable and any standard PO process timelines?
4) I'll prepare a minimal MOP (method-of-proof) checklist and an estimated infra plan for a 2-node Redwood Dedicated trial plus burst policy. Attached a blank MOP template and our one-pager so you can see the proposed flow.

Tentative dates
- PoC kickoff: week of June 7 (flexible)
- Initial trial runs: 2 weeks after kickoff

Attachments referenced
- redwood-mop-template.xlsx (MOP checklist — please fill the highlighted rows)
- redwood-one-pager.pdf (product summary and what the trial will validate)

If any of this is off, flag it and I'll update. Otherwise, if you can send the traffic sample + Prometheus queries today or tomorrow, we'll prepare the sizing and an outline MOP by Wednesday.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple clarifications and I attached the sample trace and a link to the SLA sheet.

Quick clarifications
- The p95/ p99 numbers I quoted are for the websocket streaming endpoint (v1/stream). The 1.1s p95 was during a peak test where routing CPU hit 95% and we saw batching collapse.
- Model is open-llama-9B (8-bit quant), sequence length typically 512; occasional spikes to 2048 for long sessions.
- Current batching is per-worker naive batching (we aggregate inside the process, batch size rarely exceeds 8).

Attached and links
- Attached: finlytics-sample-traces-20270522.json (small anonymized traces)
- SLA sheet (internal): https://drive.google.com/finlytics/perf-sla-spreadsheet

Procurement note
- procurement@finlytics.com: 60-day PoC is fine, but we'll need a Master Services Agreement and a standard SOW. PO lead time ~2–3 weeks once SOW is agreed.

Next steps from our side
- We'll drop the Prometheus query for p95/p99 (Grafana dashboard panel) by EOD today.
- Can you confirm Redwood's suggested config for an initial 2-node trial (CPU/GPU SKU and expected token throughput)?

Regards,
